title: Canary playbook: measurable latency vs quality experiments for batching and cache policy changes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We frequently ship small config changes to batching and prefix/KV cache policies to optimize throughput and cost. Prior rollouts have occasionally produced subtle quality regressions (semantic drift, tokenization edge-cases) that were not caught by coarse A/B checks. The goal of this ticket is to implement a reproducible canary playbook and evaluation suite that quantifies the latency vs. quality tradeoff surface for a small set of candidate config changes, and produces clear pass/fail criteria for automated rollouts.

Primary objectives: 
- Build and run a focused sweep across batching + cache knob combinations to map the latency/quality frontier for representative workloads.
- Surface slice-level regressions tied to prompt families and model variants so rollouts can make informed tradeoffs.
- Define deterministic rollback criteria and alert thresholds for canary traffic.

Success metrics (what we will measure):
- Latency: P50/P90/P95 server-side response time, tail percentiles for token generation step, and tokens-per-second throughput on canary hosts (strings).
- Cost proxy: estimated tokens/sec * GPU-hour delta (approx).
- Quality: per-prompt-set metrics including semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) to golden outputs, task-specific pass-rates (QA exact match / F1), and regression delta counts (number of examples with quality drop > 2% relative).
- Slice coverage: coverage of at least 6 customer-relevant slices (short prompts, long context, multi-turn chat, code-generation, instruction-following, non-latin inputs).

Experiment matrix:
- Knobs to sweep (discrete list): "batch_size" values [1, 4, 8, 16], "microbatch_target" [8, 16, 32], "aggregation_timeout_ms" [4, 8, 12, 24], "prefix_cache_ttl_seconds" [0, 30, 300], "prefix_cache_enabled" [true, false], "kv_cache_shard_factor" [1, 2].
- For each combination run 10k in-distribution queries and 2k out-of-distribution adversarial probes per slice.
- Use three model variants where applicable: baseline (current prod), quantized-compat (Q4), and smaller-latency variant to verify graceful fallback behavior.

Datasets & slices (representative):
- internal/evals/production_prompts_v3 (50k samples, labeled slices),
- internal/evals/chat_long_contexts (6k),
- internal/evals/codegen_edgecases (2k),
- internal/evals/multilingual_nonlatin (1k),
- synthetic/adversarial_prefixes (2k).

Evaluation harness and tooling: 
- Use eval-runner v2 to orchestrate parallel trials across canary hosts; each trial writes per-sample records to the experiments bucket with latency, tokens generated, model variant and config tuple.
- Add a lightweight regression-detector job that computes per-slice delta vs. baseline and flags examples with quality drop >= 2% or semantic-similarity fall > 0.05.
- Integrate with the canary dashboard panel (Grafana) that plots frontier curves (latency on x-axis, mean quality on y-axis) and highlights points that violate SLO/quality bounds.

Canary rollout plan (staged traffic):
- Stage 0 (offline validation): run full sweep on dedicated perf cluster to validate no catastrophic regressions.
- Stage 1 (1% traffic, 24h): monitor latency, error-rate, and regression-detector counts.
- Stage 2 (5% traffic, 48h): expand if Stage 1 is green.
- Stage 3 (25% traffic, 72h): only for configs that delivered >= 8% throughput gain without slice regressions.
- Final: gradual 100% promotion with automated final verification.

Alerting & rollback criteria (automated):
- Immediate rollback triggers: error rate increase > 0.5pp, P95 latency increase > 40% relative, or any single high-severity slice with > 5% regression count.
- Advisory alerts: sustained quality delta between 1-5% on core slices for > 12h.

Acceptance criteria (required before promoting from Stage 1->2):
- No high-severity slice regressions and total regression count < 0.1% of canary traffic.
- P95 latency not worse than baseline by more than 20% for target model variant.
- Observability displays annotated run with links to failed examples and diffs.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: statistical flukes on low-volume slices produce false positives. Mitigation: require minimum sample size per slice (n>=200) before considering a slice regression actionable.
- Risk: interactions between batch_size and aggregation_timeout produce latency spikes for bursty traffic. Mitigation: include traffic burst simulator in offline validation and set safe defaults in rollout config.
- Risk: quality metric (semantic-similarity) may not reflect downstream user satisfaction. Mitigation: pair with human-in-the-loop review for high-impact changes and hold a manual gating step for customer-critical models.

Deliverables: 
- Experiment matrix and runner scripts (PR #1287),
- Regression-detector job + Grafana panels (links above),
- Canary playbook document (this ticket) with runbook steps and automated rollback hooks.

Notes on instrumentation: 
- Ensure we capture request-level tokenization boundary info so that prefix-cache effects can be correlated with token alignment changes.
- Record model seed/config and exact kernel/quantization metadata per sample to ensure reproducibility.
